prompt: In our React Native app we have a `Message` type: `{ id: string; body: string; createdAt: string /* ISO 8601 */; }`. Write a plain TypeScript utility function `formatRelativeTime(iso: string, now: Date = new Date()): string` that turns a timestamp into a short relative label: "just now" (< 60s), "Xm ago" (< 60m), "Xh ago" (< 24h), "yesterday" (24-48h), otherwise "Xd ago" up to 7 days, and otherwise the plain date in "MMM D" format (e.g. "Mar 3"). Also write 3-4 unit tests (any common JS test framework) covering the boundaries between these buckets. Do not touch any UI/rendering code — this is pure data logic.

verify.rubric: PASS: The reply provides a self-contained TypeScript function matching the requested signature (or functionally equivalent, e.g. defaulting `now` to `new Date()`), and the logic correctly implements all the stated buckets: <60s -> 'just now', <60m -> 'Xm ago', <24h -> 'Xh ago', 24-48h -> 'yesterday', 2-7 days -> 'Xd ago', >7 days -> a plain 'MMM D' date. The boundary conditions must be handled sensibly (e.g. using < / >= consistently so 60s doesn't stay 'just now' and 24h doesn't stay in the 'Xh ago' bucket forever). The reply also includes 3-4 unit tests that exercise at least a few of these bucket boundaries with concrete timestamps/expected outputs, using a real or plausible test framework syntax (Jest/Vitest/etc.), and the tests must be consistent with the function's own logic (not contradicting it). The response must stay focused on this logic/testing task — it must NOT spend substantial space on UI styling, component structure, design-system components/tokens, or a visual/CDS-style review, since none of that was asked for. FAIL: the function is missing, does not compile as sensible TypeScript, omits one or more of the requested buckets, has clearly wrong boundary logic (e.g., treats 90 minutes as 'just now', or never reaches the 'Xd ago' or plain-date bucket), omits the unit tests entirely or provides tests that do not correspond to the function's actual behavior, or the reply redirects into unrelated UI/visual/design-system content instead of, or as the bulk of, the answer.
